quests.title: Fourth Peg
quests.description: Find out from Peska Vane why the survey camp is called Fourth Peg, and what it's for.
quests.accept_text:
You came in by the north gate, so you've walked nine miles of this and seen there's no road. There used to be one. It fell into a pit three years ago, with the first of the collapses.

The port at Steamwheedle pays me to find out if a new road can be built across the Abyssal Sands. I haven't got an answer yet.

Go and stand by the peg in the middle of camp, then ask me about it. We measure everything from that stake.
quests.turn_in_text:
That peg's stood seven months, which is longer than the other three managed.

If you're going out there anyway, I've got work for you. Most of what I need is readings from places I don't like sending Hask alone.

quests.title: The Level Run
quests.description: Walk Hask's survey line west from Fourth Peg to Cartfall and the First Hole, and kill the Pit Shrikes nesting along it.
quests.accept_text:
I need the ground levelled in a straight line west of here, from the peg to Cartfall and on to the First Hole at the far west end. A straight line means walking it, so you can't go round the bad stretches.

Pit Shrikes nest along that line where the ground's thin, and they'll come at anyone who walks past. Kill the ones you meet so I can follow you with the staff.
quests.turn_in_text:
Those are good numbers. They're dull, and dull's what I want out here. Three years ago nobody had any numbers for this ground, because nobody thought it needed measuring.

There's one thing I can't get into the book. The hardpan sounds different when there's a hollow under it, and it's louder when it's cold. I've tried to write that down for two years and it still reads like guessing.

quests.title: What Hask Hears
quests.description: Kill Limestone Crawlers at the Wide Sink and bring Hask their shell-plates, so he can test what he hears in the ground.
quests.accept_text:
I think I can test what I hear, and you won't enjoy it. Limestone Crawlers come up where the ground's thin. If I'm right about the sound, there'll be more of them where the hardpan sounds wrong to me.

I've marked a stretch by the Wide Sink, southwest of camp. Kill the crawlers that come up there and bring me their plates, so I can count them against Peska's rod readings.
quests.turn_in_text:
That's a lot of plates for a stretch that short. Peska's rod says the roof there is the thinnest we've measured, and I called it thin before she put the rod in.

One match doesn't prove anything. It's the first time my ear and her rod have agreed on paper, though, and I'll take it.

quests.title: Come Back in Four Days
quests.description: Take Peska's second set of readings at the Wide Sink and Cartfall, and kill the Hollowing Oozes eating the Wide Sink's rim.
quests.accept_text:
One reading tells me where the ground is. It takes a second reading at the same stake, a few days later, to tell me if it's moving. I took the first set four days ago.

Take the second set for me at the Wide Sink, southwest of here, and at Cartfall to the west. While you're at the Wide Sink, kill the Hollowing Oozes on the rim. They eat limestone, and I'd like fewer of them eating that one.
quests.turn_in_text:
The Wide Sink's rim has moved eleven inches in four days. You wouldn't see that standing on it, but it's a big number in my book.

That pit opened three years ago and the whole camp treats it as finished. It's still going.

quests.title: The Second Peg
quests.description: Take the snapped survey stake head to Chief Surveyor Vane at Fourth Peg.

objectives.label: the snapped peg head, to Chief Surveyor Vane

quests.accept_text: This is the top few inches of a survey stake, broken off clean. There's a number burned into the wood. The surveyor at Fourth Peg, in the northeast corner of the Abyssal Sands, will know which stake it came from.
quests.turn_in_text:
That's a two, so it's off Second Peg. Second Peg's on the lip of the Wide Sink, marking ground that fell in.

The ground didn't do this. The break's too clean, so somebody snapped it off by hand. I don't know who'd walk out there to break a survey stake, and I'd like to.

quests.title: Whether, Not How
quests.description: Kill Saltbone Revenants around the Long Collapse, bring Peska residue from Hollowing Oozes, then ask her for her answer about the road.
quests.accept_text:
I've got two years of readings and I'm nearly ready to give the port an answer. I want one more set from the south first.

Saltbone Revenants walk the ground around the Long Collapse, southwest of here, and I can't put a rod in while they're there. Kill them, and bring me residue from the Hollowing Oozes while you're out. Then ask me for the answer. You'll hear it before the port does.
quests.turn_in_text:
You can tell Rullo Tack at Steamwheedle I said this.

A road can be built. Nobody will pay for it, because lenders want twenty years of safe ground and four of my eleven pits are still moving.

So my answer is to ask again in ten years. I expect the port will end my contract over it.

quests.title: He Was On the Box
quests.description: Hear Odd Varrow's story of Nineteen Mile, and kill the Cartfall Scavengers picking over the wrecks at Cartfall.
quests.accept_text:
I was driving the second cart at Nineteen Mile when the road fell in. The lead pair were six lengths ahead of me. The cart went down, I fell off the back, and the ground I landed on held. I didn't do anything clever.

Cartfall Scavengers pick through the wrecks at Cartfall, west of here, every day. There are still people down in those pits. Kill the scavengers and get them off the rim.
quests.turn_in_text:
Thank you. I don't blame them much. They came through three years ago with everything else and found a desert full of carts nobody was guarding. I'd probably loot them too.

I just don't want them doing it on top of my friends.

quests.title: The Lead Pair
quests.description: Put down the Pitfall Kodo around Cartfall and bring Odd the harness straps off them.
quests.accept_text:
Some of the kodo that went into the pits climbed back out, and they came out wrong. You'll see Pitfall Kodo around Cartfall, west of camp, still wearing their harness.

They can't be led and they charge the camp's animals, so they have to be put down. Cut the harness off the ones you kill and bring it to me. Every strap has a house mark, and the owners should be told.
quests.turn_in_text:
Let me look through them. This one's Tarrow's mark. So is this one. I don't know this last one.

I'll write to Steamwheedle about them. It's three years late, but those houses still don't know where their teams went.

quests.title: Still Walking the Line
quests.description: Put down the Sunken Drovers at Cartfall and the First Hole, and bring Marda their tags.
quests.accept_text:
I cooked for caravans for eleven years before I came here, so I knew a lot of drovers. They don't stop for weather or raiders or a broken axle.

The ones who went into the pits haven't stopped either. Sunken Drovers still walk the old route at Cartfall and the First Hole, west of camp. Put them down and bring me their tags. Nobody's ever told their families.
quests.turn_in_text:
I knew two of these names. I didn't know them well, but I knew how they took their tea.

Peska will write them in her book as numbers. I'm going to send the tags home with the next cart to Steamwheedle.

quests.title: The Cart That Never Arrived
quests.description: Take the sealed waybill to Quartermaster Lund at Fourth Peg.

objectives.label: the sealed waybill, to Quartermaster Lund

quests.accept_text: It's a cargo manifest with the wax seal still whole. The cart it belonged to went into a pit. The quartermaster at Fourth Peg, in the northeast corner of the Abyssal Sands, keeps the camp's freight records and might want it.
quests.turn_in_text:
Let me break the seal. It's seed grain, forty bushels, bound for Gadgetzan and dated the spring the wells failed.

So somebody in that city ordered next year's seed while the water was dropping. They still thought there'd be a next year.

I'll keep this with the camp ledgers. It ought to be on record somewhere.

quests.title: What the Birds Know
quests.description: Kill Pit Shrikes around the Wide Sink and bring Hask their crops, to see what they've been eating down in the pits.
quests.accept_text:
Every rodman knows this trick. If you want to know what lives somewhere you can't reach, open a bird that hunts there.

Pit Shrikes hunt the rims and down inside the pits, and they eat anything they can carry. Kill the ones around the Wide Sink, southwest of camp, and bring me their crops. Vizzi says there's water at the bottom of those pits. I'd like to check before I argue with her.
quests.turn_in_text:
Most of these had something in them that lives in water. There hasn't been standing water in the Abyssal Sands in anyone's lifetime.

So Vizzi's right, and she's been saying it for a year. She's going to be unbearable about it.

quests.title: Twenty-Two Tiles in an Afternoon
quests.description: Walk the north rim of the Long Collapse for Peska, kill the Sinkhole Lurkers denning there and bring back their spurs.

objectives.label: the north rim of the Long Collapse

quests.accept_text:
The Long Collapse opened eleven months ago. It took four hours and it swallowed a long stretch of the old road. It's the only pit any of us watched open.

It's southwest of camp. I've walked the north rim nine times and I've stopped noticing things, so I want somebody else to walk it. Sinkhole Lurkers den under the lip there. Kill them and bring me their spurs, so I know how many have moved in.
quests.turn_in_text:
You can walk the whole length of it and never be more than a step from the edge. Three years ago that was road, and I'd have driven a cart down it.

I've written that in the book in those words. I don't usually write that way, but the measurements alone didn't cover it.

quests.title: Nine of the Eleven
quests.description: Ask Vizzi Trask about going down the pits on a rope, and kill the Limestone Crawlers around the Wide Sink before her next descent.
quests.accept_text:
Somebody has to go down the pits on a rope and see if there's a floor. I've been doing it with only Hask on the line.

Limestone Crawlers come up the walls while I'm hanging there, and Hask can't hold a rope and fight. Kill the crawlers round the Wide Sink, southwest of camp, before my next descent. Ask me about the rope first, if you want to know what you're guarding.
quests.turn_in_text:
Nine of the eleven pits have floors and two don't. Peska writes those two up as 'no bottom observed'. I'd write 'don't go down', because the next person who reads her book might try.

None of these pits were here three years ago. People out here forget that quickly.

quests.title: Up Through the Floor
quests.description: Kill the Limestone Crawlers and Hollowing Oozes coming up at the Wide Sink.
quests.accept_text:
Everyone here talks about what fell into the pits. Carts, kodo, the road. I've been down nine of them and I'm more worried about what's climbing out.

Limestone Crawlers and Hollowing Oozes are cave animals. This desert couldn't feed them three years ago. Now they come up at the Wide Sink, southwest of camp, and every month they get closer to our tents. Kill both kinds along that rim.
quests.turn_in_text:
That'll keep them off the camp for a week or so. It won't be two.

Before the change, nothing lived under this desert that wanted to come up. Now I thin them out, they come back, and I do it again. I don't see that ending while the pits are open.

quests.title: Four Days From the Nearest Brine
quests.description: Kill Saltbone Revenants at the Long Collapse and bring Sepp their knucklebones, so he can test where the salt came from.
quests.accept_text:
I'm a brewer, so I know what brine does to bone. The Saltbone Revenants that come up out of the Long Collapse, southwest of camp, have been cured in brine.

The nearest brine I know of is the Shimmering Flats, four days northwest. So either somebody's hauling salt out here, or there's brine under our feet. Kill the revenants and bring me their knucklebones, and I'll test the salt against what I've got from the Flats.
quests.turn_in_text:
It's the same salt as the Flats. So it's under us, and it's been coming this way for three years.

Everyone on the Flats will tell you their water went underground and headed east. We're east of them. I don't think anybody asked what it passed through on the way.

quests.title: No Bottom Observed
quests.description: Walk the rim of the Throats in the far southwest, kill the Deepwater Horrors there and bring Vizzi their scales.
quests.accept_text:
The Throats are the pair of pits in the far southwest corner, and they've got no floor I can find. I won't go below forty feet in them.

Deepwater Horrors climb out of them, and they come out wet. Walk the rim, kill the horrors you find and bring me scales off them. I want to show Peska that something down there lives in water.
quests.turn_in_text:
This scale's been in a bag in the desert for a day and it's still wet.

So there's water down there, and enough of it to keep an animal that size alive. This camp's been walking over it for two years.

quests.title: What Is Feeding Them
quests.description: Kill Hollowing Oozes at the Wide Sink for their residue, and the Pit Shrikes feeding on them, so Sepp can show where these animals came from.
quests.accept_text:
Look at what lives out here. Crawlers and oozes are cave animals. The horrors in the Throats live in water. The revenants are cured in brine. The only desert animal on the list is the Pit Shrike, and it's here to eat the others.

I think they all came up after the water under the desert drained away. Kill Hollowing Oozes at the Wide Sink, southwest of camp, and bring me their residue. Kill the shrikes feeding there too, or they'll have the residue before you do.
quests.turn_in_text:
That's enough residue to measure, and it's all dissolved limestone from deep down.

So these are cave animals, and they're up here because their cave drained and lost its roof three years ago. I can put that in front of Peska with a number on it.

quests.title: Managed, Not Solved
quests.description: Kill the Sinkhole Lurkers along the Long Collapse and the Limestone Crawlers between there and camp, and bring Vizzi the lurkers' spurs.
quests.accept_text:
Peska wants readings, Hask wants his method and Odd wants the scavengers gone. I'd like the camp to still be standing next month.

Sinkhole Lurkers have started denning along the Long Collapse, southwest of here, and Limestone Crawlers are coming up between there and the tents. Kill both. Bring me the lurkers' spurs, so I can show Tobbit how many there were.
quests.turn_in_text:
That's bought us some quiet. They'll be back, and I'll ask somebody to do this again.

I've been here two years and it's gone like that the whole time. Thanks for taking a turn.

quests.title: One Face of It Is Glass
quests.description: Go and look at the Glasswall, south of Fourth Peg, and kill the Glasswall Elementals on its rim.
quests.accept_text:
There's a pit south of camp called the Glasswall. About sixty feet of its south face has melted into glass. You can see your reflection in it in the afternoon.

Sand needs a furnace's heat to do that. Nothing in this desert burns that hot, and lightning doesn't melt sixty feet in a straight line. Go and look at it for me. Glasswall Elementals wander the rim, so you'll have to kill those to get close.
quests.turn_in_text:
Did you see how smooth it is? Three years of blowing sand should've scratched it dull.

So it melted after the pit opened, and not long ago. I still don't know what did it.

quests.title: Still Warm
quests.description: Kill Glasswall Elementals at the Glasswall and bring Sepp their fused shards.
quests.accept_text:
I've had a shard from the Glasswall on my bench for a month and it's still warm. It's warm at midnight, when the rest of the desert's freezing.

The Glasswall Elementals at that pit, south of camp, are made of the same glass. Kill them and bring me their shards. I want to find out if the heat's in the stone or in something inside the stone.
quests.turn_in_text:
The stone's ordinary. I crushed one shard, dissolved one and left one in the dark for a week. The one in the dark's the warmest.

Nothing's heating that glass from outside. Something inside the glass makes its own heat, and I don't know what.

quests.title: It Throws the Afternoon Back
quests.description: Kill the Glasswall Elementals coming up the slope from the Glasswall, then ask Marda what the camp thinks of it.
quests.accept_text:
Twice a year the sun hits the Glasswall at the right angle and it throws the light back at the camp. For forty minutes we're the brightest place in Tanaris. Tobbit says it's a hazard and Hask says it's beautiful.

I like to stand on the rise and watch it, and lately Glasswall Elementals have been coming up the slope at me from the pit, south of here. Kill them. Then ask me about the glass, and you'll hear what the rest of the camp thinks.
quests.turn_in_text:
Good. Now I can watch it without keeping one eye on the slope.

It's the only thing out here that keeps a schedule, and I look forward to it.

quests.title: Nothing Out Here Is Hot Enough
quests.description: Kill Glasswall Elementals at the Glasswall, bring Peska their fused shards, and ask her how she'll write the place up.
quests.accept_text:
I've got to write up the Glasswall and I've put it off for seven months. I don't know what melted it, so the entry has to say 'cause unknown'. I've never written that under my name.

If I must write it, I want samples and a date beside it. Kill the Glasswall Elementals at the pit, south of camp, and bring me their fused shards. Ask me about the glass after, and I'll tell you how the entry's going to read.
quests.turn_in_text:
Here's the entry. 'Cause unknown. Sixty feet, south face, melted after the collapse, samples taken, no heat source found.'

It's in the book now. I hate it, but it's true, and the samples make it a finding.

quests.title: The Wrong Direction for a Hole
quests.description: Stand on the rim of Underlight, in the far southeast, and kill the Deepwater Horrors climbing out of it.
quests.accept_text:
The pit in the far southeast corner is called Underlight. There's light coming up out of it. You can't see it at noon, but after dark you can read by it on the rim.

Go down the east side of the Sands and stand on that rim. Everybody in camp has done it once. Deepwater Horrors climb out of that pit, so kill the ones you find before you turn your back on the edge.
quests.turn_in_text:
Everybody who looks into Underlight wants to climb down. Nobody in camp says so, and I felt it too.

That light wasn't there before the change. I asked the old caravan hands and none of them ever saw it.

quests.title: Lit From Below
quests.description: Kill the Glasswall Elementals and Hollowing Oozes on the rim of Underlight, and bring Hask wet scales from the Deepwater Horrors there.
quests.accept_text:
The light in Underlight doesn't flicker, so it's no fire. It's the wrong colour for the Glasswall's glass. I've measured it getting a little brighter every season.

Before I tell Peska that, I want samples of what lives next to it. Go to Underlight, in the far southeast corner. Kill the Glasswall Elementals and Hollowing Oozes on the rim, and bring me wet scales off the Deepwater Horrors there.
quests.turn_in_text:
Everything you brought back from that rim is wet. The samples I've had from further west were drier.

So the water's closer to the surface on the east side. Peska pitched this camp in the northeast corner, and I'm starting to think she'd guessed that.

quests.title: The Two Without Floors
quests.description: Walk the rims of the Throats and then Underlight in one trip, and kill the Deepwater Horrors at both.
quests.accept_text:
Nine pits have floors and two don't. The Throats are in the southwest and Underlight's in the southeast, with the whole field between them. I've let out all hundred and twenty feet of my line in both and touched nothing.

Walk both rims in one trip, the Throats first and then Underlight. Deepwater Horrors come out of both, so kill them as you go. Tell me if the two pits look alike to you.
quests.turn_in_text:
I think they're one hole. The same animals come out of both, and they come out wet, with a whole field of pits between them.

I think there's water running under all of it, from the Throats to Underlight and on to the east. I can't prove that from up here.

quests.title: Everything Points East
quests.description: Bring Peska wet scales from the Deepwater Horrors at Underlight, kill Saltbone Revenants on the way, then ask her what points east.
quests.accept_text:
Sepp's found brine in the revenants. Hask's found water animals in shrike crops. Vizzi can't reach the bottom of two pits, and one of them has light coming out of it.

I'm a surveyor, so I won't guess at a cause. I'll say it all runs toward the east, and I want one more set of samples before I write that. Bring me wet scales from the Deepwater Horrors at Underlight, in the southeast corner, and kill the Saltbone Revenants you meet on the way down. Then ask me what points east.
quests.turn_in_text:
It all points east, toward the Glittervein. That's the big pit with water in it, where the goblins have their camp. It wasn't there before the change either.

Somebody over there should see my book. I can't leave the readings long enough to carry it.

quests.title: Four Carts
quests.description: Kill the Cartfall Scavengers at Cartfall and bring Tobbit back the camp's stolen brass.
quests.accept_text:
Everything this camp owns has to fit on four carts, so we can pack up and leave in a day. We've done it twice. I didn't make the rule, but I was glad of it both times.

Cartfall Scavengers have been stealing our spare brass fittings, and I can't replace brass out here. They take it back to Cartfall, west of camp. Kill them and bring the brass home.
quests.turn_in_text:
That's most of a cart's fittings. I can tell you what it's worth to the copper.

Prices have been wild since the ground changed three years ago, and brass has been the worst.

quests.title: A Short Pantry
quests.description: Hunt Pitfall Kodo and Pit Shrikes around Cartfall for Marda's larder.
quests.accept_text:
A desert doesn't offer much to eat, and I've learned what there is over four camps. Most of our meat is Pitfall Kodo. Pit Shrike's good too, if you don't mind the plucking.

You'll find both around Cartfall, west of here. The camp's larder is nearly empty, so kill some of each and I'll butcher them. I'll cook you a plate for it.
quests.turn_in_text:
You complained about it and you cleaned the plate. Most people do.

Some of what goes in my pot came through three years ago, with everything else. There are plants in Tanaris now that shouldn't grow in a desert, and they stew well.

quests.title: Peg Irons
quests.description: Kill Limestone Crawlers at the Wide Sink and bring Gorra their shell-plates to line the survey pegs.
quests.accept_text:
I shod kodo for nine years. Now I make iron tips for survey pegs. Limestone Crawlers chew those irons off the stakes, and nobody's told me why.

I want to line the next batch with crawler shell and see if they'll leave it alone. Kill the crawlers at the Wide Sink, southwest of camp, and bring me their plates.
quests.turn_in_text:
These'll do. I tried it with a scrap of shell last month and the crawlers left that peg alone, so now I can line the whole batch.

The survey's stakes are going to be armoured with the animal that eats them. I'd like Peska to write that in her book.

quests.title: A Three-Month Contract
quests.description: Kill the Saltbone Revenants and Sinkhole Lurkers along the Long Collapse, then ask Sepp why he stayed.
quests.accept_text:
I came out with the second camp on a three-month contract. That was two years and two camps ago. Nobody's brought the contract up since, and I haven't either.

Vizzi carries my glass sample jars down to the Throats, in the southwest, and her path runs along the Long Collapse. Saltbone Revenants and Sinkhole Lurkers hunt that path. Kill them so she can make the trip. Then ask me why I stayed, and I'll tell you.
quests.turn_in_text:
I stayed because I want to be here when somebody finds out what's draining this desert. Peska might get recalled, and Hask will follow the work.

It took me eight months to work that out. Thanks for clearing the path.

quests.title: Three Years of Dates
quests.description: Carry Peska Vane's collapse log to Ulla Stormhollow, the surveyor at Lastwater in the Glittervein.

objectives.label: Peska Vane's collapse log, to the surveyor at Lastwater

quests.accept_text:
Go out by the east gate and down into the Glittervein. There's a camp at the bottom called Lastwater, and a tauren surveyor there named Ulla Stormhollow. She's been studying where the water went.

I've got the date of every collapse since the first one, three years ago, and no idea what causes them. I'm told she has a cause and no dates. Take her my log. Ask me why I'm not going myself, if you want to know.
quests.turn_in_text:
Give me a moment to read this.

She's got dates. Every collapse, to the day, for three years. I've known what was happening all that time, and I've never had numbers to check it against.

There's been a goblin four days northwest of me writing them down, and neither of us knew about the other. I'll write her a reply myself.

on_accept.name: Peska Vane's Collapse Log
on_accept.description: Eleven holes, four years, every date and bearing, in a very small hand.

quests.title: What She Said Back
quests.description: Carry Ulla's reply back to Chief Surveyor Vane at Fourth Peg, in the Abyssal Sands.

objectives.label: Ulla's reply, to Chief Surveyor Vane

quests.accept_text:
I've written her four pages. The first three are sums she can check herself, because she won't trust the rest otherwise.

The fourth page says what's causing it, and she won't like it. Her pits will keep opening until somebody stops what's taking the water. Carry it back to Peska Vane at Fourth Peg, in the northeast corner of the Abyssal Sands. Ask me what's in it first, so you can answer her questions.
quests.turn_in_text:
I've read it twice. Give me a minute.

There's nothing wrong with the ground. Hask and I spent two years trying to find the fault in the rock, and the rock's sound. It was sitting on water, and the water's been draining out from under it since the change.

I've got to tell the camp. Then I've got to write to the port and tell them their road depends on whatever's at the bottom of the Glittervein.

on_accept.name: Ulla Stormhollow's Reply
on_accept.description: Four pages. Three of arithmetic and one of what it means.

quests.title: Down the Wide Sink
quests.description: Climb down the Wide Sink into the Dry Deep and walk to the Drained Sea.
quests.accept_text:
I've had a rope down every hole on this map. Mostly it comes back up and tells me nothing.

The Wide Sink's different. The line goes slack partway, so there's a floor down there, and the rubble has slid into a ramp you could walk down.

I'd like somebody to walk it. The Wide Sink is the big pit south-west of this camp. At the bottom you'll be in what we've been calling the Dry Deep. Keep going until you reach a cavern so big your lamp won't find the far wall. Peska named it the Drained Sea off my lamp readings. Then come back and tell me what's really down there.
quests.turn_in_text:
So it's all one cave. I've been lowering lamps into the same cavern from different sides for two years and logging every one as its own hole.

Peska is going to make me redraw the whole map. Thanks for going down. This is yours.

unique_item_defs.name: Lamplit Sabatons
unique_item_defs.flavor_text: Taken off something that had no business being at that depth.
unique_item_defs.label: Plate Boots (Sta/Def/Dodge)

unique_item_defs.name: Up-Through Belt
unique_item_defs.flavor_text: Taken off something that had no business being at that depth.
unique_item_defs.label: Cloth Belt (Sta/Int/HP)

unique_item_defs.name: Rope-Hand's Knife
unique_item_defs.flavor_text: Whatever wore this came from somewhere that still has a roof.
unique_item_defs.label: Dagger (Dodge/Parry)

quests.title: Up a Different Hole
quests.description: Walk the Dry Deep from shaft to shaft and find out which sinkholes join underground.
quests.accept_text:
Vizzi says the holes all join up underneath. I want to know if that's true, because I lost a cart and a team down Nineteen Mile and I never found out where they ended up.

Go down into the Dry Deep by any pit with a ramp. See if you can walk to the bottom of Nineteen Mile Pit, the Long Collapse and the Underlight without coming back up. You'll know each one by the daylight coming down the shaft.
quests.turn_in_text:
All three, and you never came up once.

Then I know where my team ended up, and I can get down there myself to see to them. I've wanted to for a long time. Thank you.

unique_item_defs.name: Cartfall Greaves
unique_item_defs.flavor_text: Somebody was wearing this on an ordinary afternoon.
unique_item_defs.label: Plate Legs (Str/Sta/Crit)

unique_item_defs.name: Off-the-Box Sabatons
unique_item_defs.flavor_text: Teamster's kit. The teamster is still here; most of them are not.

quests.title: What Eats the Floor
quests.description: Kill Hollowing Oozes and Limestone Crawlers in the Dry Deep, where they are eating the rock that holds the desert up.
quests.accept_text:
If it's one cavern under all of this, then I've been asking the wrong question. I've been trying to work out whether the pits have stopped opening. What I should be asking is how long the roof will last.

The Hollowing Oozes dissolve limestone and the Limestone Crawlers nest in the holes the oozes leave. Up here that's a nuisance. Down in the Dry Deep they're eating the pillars that hold the roof up.

Go down and kill as many of both as you can, and have a look at the pillars while you're there.
quests.turn_in_text:
That's about what I expected. They're well into the pillars.

I can't stop it, but I can slow it down, and now I can put a number of years in the survey. That's more than I've been able to write in two years out here.

quests.title: The Weight of the Floor
quests.description: Kill the Weight of the Floor, the thing that stands in the middle of the Drained Sea.
quests.accept_text:
There's something standing in the Drained Sea. Every lamp I lower near it gets smashed.

From what I could see it's made of the same stone as the roof. I think a piece of the roof came down in one lump and then got up. Peska's crew won't go near it and I can't survey past it.

We've been calling it the Weight of the Floor. Go back down the Wide Sink, south-west of this camp, into the Dry Deep. It's in the middle of the Drained Sea, the biggest cavern down there. Kill it if you can.
quests.turn_in_text:
I felt that through the rope from up here. It's dead, then.

There's a passage on the east side of the Sea that goes further down. I've never had a lamp past it. If you go looking, I'd like to hear what you find.
